author: Hussain Nasser
headline: Venture building × AI × games in Saudi Arabia | PE & M&A modelling and valuation | Portfolio Manager, Revival Lab | Investment Director, Glo
text:
Nearly 200 of Uber's driverless cars will be on UAE roads by year-end.

Uber expects about 700 worldwide by then, so that's more than a quarter of the fleet in one country.

Two things I noticed in Uber's Q3 remarks:

1. The plan is over 2,000 driverless vehicles by the end of 2027, roughly half in the US and half outside it.

2. Uber says its focus is moving from partnerships and testing to driverless commercial service. The next test is how much each car is used and what it earns.

For Gulf investors, I think this is now a fleet business. Someone has to buy the cars, finance them, keep them on the road and run the depots. That's where I'd look for local companies to build.

If you work in mobility here, which part of the fleet would you want to own?

Sources: Uber Q3 2026 prepared remarks and earnings call (4 Nov 2026)

author: Hussain Nasser
headline: Venture building × AI × games in Saudi Arabia | PE & M&A modelling and valuation | Portfolio Manager, Revival Lab | Investment Director, Glo
text:
Emaar is offering AED 15 a share for the part of Emaar Development it doesn't own. Is that a 3% premium or a 149% premium?

Both. It depends on which start date you pick. The slides show all five.

From Emaar's offer page:
vs the 2017 subscription price (AED 6.03): +148.8%
vs the 1-week average price: +21.7%
vs the 2 Nov close: +19.4%
vs the 3-month average price: +15.7%
vs the 5 Nov close: +3.3%

Two things I'd look at:

1. 2 Nov was the last trading day before the board announcement. I'd measure from there: 19.4%.

2. After the news the share closed at AED 14.52 on 5 Nov. From that price the offer adds 3.3%.

Emaar already holds just over 79%. The offer is open until 10 December.

Which price do you use to judge a buyout premium?

Sources: Emaar Properties; Enterprise AM; Gulf News
#VentureCapital #GCC #SaudiArabia #MergersAndAcquisitions #PrivateEquity #UAE

author: Claude AI
headline: 39,658 followers
text:
I stopped writing prompts in Claude. I type "/" now.

Every task I used to re-explain from scratch is a command.

/grill-me → asks the right questions before it builds anything
/delete-ai-words → cuts the phrasing that makes text sound like AI
/linkedin-hook → 10 opening lines, I pick one
/client-brief → CRM, email and web pulled into one prospect summary
/meeting-notes → recording in, next steps out
/fact-checker → every claim checked against the original source
/handoff → saves context so the next chat picks up where this one ended

25 in total. Full list in the GIF.

Here's the part that matters:

None of these are hacks. Each one is a Skill: a short file that tells Claude how I want a job done. Written once, reused every day, shared with the team.

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐩𝐫𝐨𝐦𝐩𝐭 𝐲𝐨𝐮 𝐫𝐞𝐰𝐫𝐢𝐭𝐞 𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐫𝐲 𝐌𝐨𝐧𝐝𝐚𝐲 𝐢𝐬 𝐚 𝐒𝐤𝐢𝐥𝐥 𝐲𝐨𝐮 𝐡𝐚𝐯𝐞𝐧'𝐭 𝐰𝐫𝐢𝐭𝐭𝐞𝐧 𝐲𝐞𝐭.
